summary: Tail 429s observed for dedicated tenant after autoscaling scale-down and subsequent warmup
description: Customer reports a burst of persistent 429 responses for a subset of requests that started ~10 minutes after their dedicated pool scaled down and then scaled back up for warmup. Behavior appears as 'tail' 429s rather than a total outage: a small percentage (~6-8%) of requests intermittently receive 429 while most succeed. Customer uses concurrent short-lived streaming sessions and parallel batch prefetch workers.
impact: AtlasSearch indexing pipelines experience ~6-8% failed requests which causes retries and delayed indexing. Customer reports visible backfill slowness and increased costs due to retry loops. No data loss reported. Business impact: high for nightly ingest windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has dedicated pool with autoscaling min_replicas=2 max_replicas=8 and aggressive scale-down cooldown of 90s.
2) During low load the pool scales down to 2 replicas; later traffic spikes trigger scale-up to 6 replicas for warmup.
3) Immediately after scale-up, customer runs hundreds of short streaming sessions and parallel prefetch workers that open and close frequently.
4) Within 5-15 minutes after the scale event, ~6-8% of requests receive 429s intermittently for a 12-20 minute window.
5) Issue subsides as token/concurrency buckets fully replenish and KV/prefix caches repopulate.
logs: Collected sampling of request headers and 429 response bodies attached in ticket attachments (redacted). Gate logs show 429 responses with reason field 'token_quota_exhausted' and occasional 'concurrency_window_penalty'. Scheduling logs indicate a batch-split operation and many short TCP connections. Serving-runtime logs show KV cache misses and increased cold-start latencies for some workers.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: interplay of three mechanisms: (1) token-based per-tenant bucket that is slower to replenish after scale events due to credit propagation delays, (2) concurrency window penalties applied to tenants that exceed short-lived session thresholds, and (3) KV/prefix cache coldness causing higher per-request cost and increased effective token consumption. Observed correlation between scale-downs that shorten worker TTLs and frequency of short-lived sessions. Reproduced in staging by simulating rapid connect/disconnect patterns and aggressive autoscaling cooldowns — saw similar transient 429 spike. Checked scheduler telemetry: credit refill RPCs from control-plane to new workers were delayed ~8-12s under high control-plane load, causing temporary under-accounted tokens on some workers.

resolution: Workaround provided and validated: customer increased dedicated pool min_replicas from 2 to 4 and enabled prewarm replicas for the nightly ingest window which significantly reduced the tail 429 rate. Engineering created PR to batch token-credit propagation and to relax short-session concurrency penalty during warmup windows.
